title: OKRLab — Daily Deltas & Micro‑Rituals (scratch)
content:
Purpose / short note to self:
- This is my compact daily delta log + tiny rituals scratchpad for the quarter. Not a polished playbook — a working notebook to capture micro shifts that move OKR metrics by small, frequent wins.

Quick framing (what I care about):
- Outcome: move MQL->activated conversion from 18% to 24% for the hosted-api trial flow by EOW quarter.
- Personal lead measures I can influence this sprint: two product experiments per week, daily outreach to 3 trial users, and two prompt-eval sessions per week.

How to use this page (my current plan):
- AM: write one micro-commit for the day (30–90 minutes) and record the morning delta.
- PM: capture the evening delta (what changed, what blocked), and one tiny ritual to seed tomorrow (5–15 min).
- Weekly: roll up daily deltas into a 2–3 bullet summary and a single experiment hypothesis.

Template — Daily entry (keep it terse):
- Date: YYYY-MM-DD
- Morning intention: (one line)
- Delta (AM): what I started, any early signal (metric/feedback)
- Delta (PM): what I shipped, quick qualitative result, blockers
- Tiny ritual for tomorrow: fixed, short action

Example entries (real-ish):
- 2024-11-20
  - Morning intention: segment trial emails to enterprise leads with short CTA test.
  - Delta (AM): drafted two subject lines, pulled list from Beta sheet; opened 6 threads to trial owners.
  - Delta (PM): sent segmented batch (n=28), 3 opens in first hour, 1 reply asking for walkthrough. Blocker: no up-to-date demo script — need 10m walkthrough template.
  - Tiny ritual: write 10‑slide one-page demo script (10–15m).

- 2024-11-28
  - Morning intention: evaluate prompt set A vs B for onboarding completion.
  - Delta (AM): ran eval locally on 50 samples, B had 12% higher successful intent detection.
  - Delta (PM): iterated B with lighter system prompt, improved recall slightly but hurt specificity. Blocker: limited eval set coverage.
  - Tiny ritual: add 40 more onboarding transcripts to eval bench (15–30m).

Hypotheses I'm testing (scratch format):
- H1: Short, action-oriented CTAs in trial emails increase activation within 72h (test: CTA A vs CTA B, metric: activated/triaged within 72h).
- H2: A 3-step guided onboarding flow reduces early churn more than a single generic doc (test: cohort A guided flow, cohort B generic).
- H3: Weekly prompt calibration reduces hallucination rate for templated replies by >20% (test: baseline prompts vs calibrated).

Micro-ritual library (pick 1 each day):
- 8–12 minute focused triage: triage 10 trial feedback items and flag 3 actionables.
- Demo script compose: write the 1‑pager walkthrough (10–15 minutes).
- Eval boost: add 20 samples to the bench and rerun key prompt tests (15 minutes).
- Outreach burst: send 3 tailored outreach messages to trial accounts and follow up in 48h.
- Quick postmortem: write 2 sentences on why a failed experiment failed and one learning (5 min).

Signals I track informally here (not authoritative metrics):
- activation-rate (trial -> activated) — daily sample size note if >20 trials that day
- qualitative replies / demo requests — counted as strong signals
- eval delta on key prompts (absolute % change)

Weekly rollup example (for Friday notes):
- Week of 2024-11-25
  - Wins: shipped segmented email; CTA B beat baseline (open rate +8%, activation +3% in 72h sample).
  - Learnings: smaller eval sets overfit; need broader transcripts for onboarding tests.
  - Next experiment: run guided onboarding A/B on next trial cohort (n>=60).

Current blockers / parking lot (explicit asks):
- Need a 10m demo script template from Solutions (ask @Ivy).
- Engineering: small analytics flag to tag trial cohorts (JIRA OKR-1421) — follow up with SRE/Analytics.
- Data: more annotated onboarding transcripts — ask Customer Success for 40 more (Slack thread pinned).

Unresolved questions / prompts to self (items I revisit each week):
- Is the activation metric stable enough day-to-day to trust 72h windows? If not, shift to 7d.
- Am I prioritizing outreach vs product experiments in the right ratio? (Current guess: 60/40 experiments to outreach)
- Where are my diminishing returns? Stop repeating experiments with noisy samples.

Quick action plan for next 3 workdays: (very tactical)
- Day 1: finalize demo script; send segmented email; follow up on 3 replies.
- Day 2: run guided onboarding A/B on next 30 trials; collect metadata tags.
- Day 3: analyze A/B, iterate prompt set if early signal positive.

Notes-to-self style:
- If an experiment is noisy, add sample diversity before re-running.
- Capture the one sentence learning after each experiment — makes retro summaries non-terrible.
- Keep rituals under 20 minutes. The point is repetition, not perfection.

References / quick links I hit from here:
- Confluence: okrlab-playbook-2024 (reading list for onboarding experiment patterns)
- JIRA: OKR-1421 (analytics flag for trial cohorts)
- Slack: #personal-okrs (daily check-ins, ping Maya for demo script)

Last three tiny deltas (trace):
- 2024-12-01 AM: intention=outreach burst; DM'd 3 trial owners, 1 reply scheduled.
- 2024-12-01 PM: shipped 1‑pager demo; follow-up set for Thu.
- 2024-12-02 AM: intention=eval boost; added 20 transcripts to bench and reran prompt set A/B. Early signal: A improving recall by 4%.

End note (coaching voice):
- Focus on creating a steady cadence of small changes and documenting their one-line outcome. The compound effect of many tiny deltas matters more than a few large swings.

- [ ] Run onboarding guided flow A/B with n>=60 (next week)

-- Kevin
